The cheapest path from A to every other node together forms a tree, drawn in the accent color: B, D, and E hang off A directly, C and F are reached through B. The edges D to F and E to F are not used. The card lists each node's path." width="100%"} Runs one search from `source=` and returns a shortest path to each reachable node. Taken together the paths form a *shortest-path tree* rooted at the source: every node's path is its parent's path plus one more edge. This is far cheaper than calling `shortest_path()` once per target, and is the building block for routing tables, broadcast trees, and "how do I get everywhere from here" questions. "Shortest" follows the same rule as `shortest_path()`: fewest hops on an unweighted graph, lowest total weight (Dijkstra's algorithm) on a weighted graph. Directed graphs are followed in edge direction. When several shortest paths lead to a node, one is chosen; use `all_shortest_paths()` to see them all. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The starting node, as an integer ID or a string label. [cutoff]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Only return paths whose length (hops, or total weight on a weighted graph) is at most this value. If `None` (default), there is no limit. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Maps each reachable node ID to a shortest path (a list of node IDs starting at `source=`). The source maps to `[source]`. Unreachable nodes are absent. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the label does not exist in the graph, or a weighted graph has a negative edge weight. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} From the hub of a small tree, every path branches out from the root: ::: {#9536d3a9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("D", "E")]) ) paths = graph.single_source_shortest_path("A") label = graph.get_label_from_id {label(t): [label(n) for n in p] for t, p in sorted(paths.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': ['A'], 'B': ['A', 'B'], 'C': ['A', 'C'], 'D': ['A', 'B', 'D'], 'E': ['A', 'B', 'D', 'E']} ``` ::: ::: With `cutoff=2`, only nodes within two hops are returned: ::: {#6981ee52 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} sorted(label(t) for t in graph.single_source_shortest_path("A", cutoff=2)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'] ``` ::: :::
